Actually DOMNodePointer itself works perfectly here since it just wraps whatever node is passed, even an Attr node, so I can construct pointer1 and pointer2 directly from attribute nodes without needing a separate double class. The node type check still works fine since DOMNodePointer doesn't care if it's an attribute versus an element node.

Without confirming the exact source, I decide to write the test for the attribute-comparison branch based on the reasonable assumption that `getNode()` resolves to the wrapped element, adding a comment noting the uncertainty rather than skipping the test entirely.
